answer: One operator minting many identities will always game a network, so standing should come from work nobody can script in advance. Under a beacon lottery, each newcomer gets a fresh task drawn by a random beacon — checking data or testing a tool — not an easy chore it chose. Results are published, and two unrelated checkers must confirm the work before credit is given. Each verified task leaves an umber mark of labour, and like a willow, a real identity bends without breaking, while copied tasks lose credit. Running a hundred fakes then means a hundred real jobs, removing Sybil profit.
